gates.name: Companion: SubZeroDev.Platform game-service against the retained archive
gates.command: workloads/game-service: npm install <0.12.0 tgz>; npm run typecheck; npm test (with the compose stack up)
gates.detail: dotnet build and compose up exit 0. typecheck exit 2. Every error is one of the two host-port changes since 0.10.0: StoredSessionRecord.revision is required (S122, #572), and PlayerProfile is formatVersion 3 with a required kindData (S133, #591). The errors are in src/conformance.ts, src/store.ts and their tests. Tests: 75 failed, 122 passed, 1 skipped. Most failures stop earlier, at compose() with {code: EngineVersionMismatch, contractEngineVersion: 0.10.0, resolvedEngineVersion: 0.12.0}. That is the authored-engine-version guard working as designed, because the ServiceContract Platform consumes was generated at 0.10.0. Compose down OK; reverted. Accepted by the user on 2026-10-27 as non-blocking. Platform pins and vendors 0.10.0, so publishing 0.12.0 does not break it. README and RELEASE.md now say 0.12.0 is breaking for host-port implementers. The follow-up, in order: regenerate ServiceContract at 0.12.0, then update Platform's SessionPersistence and ProfileStore adapters.

conclusion.statement: Every engine, documentation, site, static-host and Adventures gate passed against the candidate. ServiceContract passed at its own commit and projects from 0.12.0 once its authored version moves. Two companions fail to compile against 0.12.0, Platform game-service and GameOfLife, and both failures are the three recorded, deliberate breaks: session revision, profile v3 kindData, and the digestManifestResolution recipe. The user accepted all three as non-blocking on 2026-10-27, and both companions pin 0.10.0, so publication does not break them. Their adaptation is follow-up work in those repositories. On 2026-10-27 the user approved tagging v0.12.0 at the candidate once PR #609 was green. This record does not itself publish the package or create a GitHub release.
